record.paper_title: Current Unsolved Problems in Planetary Nebulae Research
record.original_question: What is the origin of the compact disks or torus-like structures found around some planetary-nebula central stars and in bipolar systems, and how, if at all, do those disks or accretion structures generate or collimate the directional outflows that shape narrow-waist bipolar or multipolar nebulae?

evidence.quote: The origin of these disks is not known.
Currently, the physical origin of the directional outflows and the collimating mechanisms are unknown.
However, the origin of such disks is uncertain.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Around the central stars of certain planetary nebulae, and in the equatorial regions of various bipolar and multipolar planetary nebulae, observations reveal compact gaseous/dusty disks or torus-like structures, often accompanied by directional (jet-like) outflows that appear to shape the host nebula into narrow-waist bipolar or multipolar morphologies.

(a) Identify the physical mechanism(s) responsible for the formation of these compact circumstellar disks and torus-like structures. Specifically, determine which of the following processes (or which combination thereof) accounts for their existence: (i) Roche-lobe overflow and accretion in a binary system containing the post-AGB primary; (ii) common-envelope evolution and its ejecta; (iii) tidal disruption or engulfment of a sub-stellar or planetary companion; (iv) wind-Roche-lobe overflow; (v) magnetically channelled mass loss from a single rotating AGB/post-AGB star; or (vi) some other process.

(b) Determine whether and how such disks (or related accretion structures) generate and collimate the observed directional outflows. In particular, specify the launching mechanism (e.g., magneto-centrifugal disk winds, magnetic-tower jets, radiation- or line-driven jets, accretion-powered outflows, or hydrodynamic focusing by an equatorial density enhancement of a wide spherical fast wind as in generalized interacting-stellar-winds models), and quantitatively relate the disk properties (mass, size, lifetime, magnetic field, accretion rate) to the resulting outflow's velocity, mass-loss rate, opening angle, and degree of collimation needed to produce the observed narrow-waist bipolar or multipolar nebular morphologies.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent observational surveys (e.g., the PANORAMA survey, JWST observations of NGC 6720) and theoretical work continue to investigate the origin of compact disks around post-AGB and planetary-nebula central stars and the connection to collimated outflows. While binary interactions (Roche-lobe overflow, common-envelope evolution, tidal engulfment) and magneto-centrifugal disk-launched jets are leading candidate mechanisms, no single mechanism has been definitively established and the precise physics of disk formation and outflow collimation in these systems remains an active and unresolved research topic.

status_evidence.title: High-Speed Outflows and Dusty Disks during the AGB to PN Transition: The PANORAMA survey
status_evidence.snippet: Survey results show bipolar/multipolar high-velocity outflows, dense toroidal waists, and disks around transitioning post-AGB stars; the linkage to binarity and collimation mechanisms is still being investigated.
status_evidence.claim: Origin of disks and collimation of outflows in post-AGB/PN systems remains an active research question.

status_evidence.title: Bipolar Planetary Nebulae from Outflow Collimation by Common Envelope Evolution
status_evidence.snippet: Common envelope ejecta supply the high pole-to-equator density contrast that allows a spherical fast wind to be focused into a bipolar outflow.
status_evidence.claim: Common-envelope-based collimation is one proposed but not uniquely established mechanism.

status_evidence.title: The structure of jets launched from post-AGB binary systems
status_evidence.snippet: Jets in post-AGB binaries are associated with accretion disks around the companion; their launching and collimation are still being modelled.
status_evidence.claim: Disk-launched jets in post-AGB binaries are studied but not fully characterized.

status_evidence.title: JWST observations of the Ring Nebula (NGC 6720): III. A dusty disk around its Central Star
status_evidence.snippet: JWST detection of a dusty disk around the central star of the Ring Nebula; origin discussed in terms of binary interaction.
status_evidence.claim: Recent observations continue to discover central-star disks whose origin is debated.
